tasks.note: The coordinator granted the worker a scope extension during the phase: the opportunity producer module and its composition wiring, because the complete Slice B gate needs a running path and Phase 18 report names the producer as Phase 19 Slice B, plus one controls route that persists the proactive opt-in and the pause flag in the existing settings key/value table, because the plan requires the proactive opt-in to be exposed and a toggle nothing reads is a fake control. The deletion of PERSISTENT intelligence was refused: design section 16 wants it but the contract review assigns the deletion of persistent intelligence to the retention phase, Phase 20, so Phase 19 exposes the served dismissals and records the deletion as a Phase 20 input. The coordinator granted the worker two more Phase 18 files for exactly one fix: the observations GET paired the FIRST workflow per subject instead of the ACTIONABLE one, and the POST started a new review workflow even when one was already live, so the served intent vanished after an acknowledgement and every review cycle leaked a workflow row. It was verified in a real browser against the running app: three workflows for one observation with its intent never served. The fix pairs the actionable workflow, serves the observation review state, and refuses to start a second workflow while one is live. The coordinator granted the Phase 18 routes test to Phase 19 as well, because the granted observations-route fix refuses a duplicate review start and the Phase 18 authentication case posted a review for an observation that already carried one. The worker adapted the FIXTURE - it seeds a second observation that carries no review and posts to that - and the assertion count is unchanged at 89, so no assertion was removed or weakened.

tasks.note: undefined The coordinator granted one more file, apps/web/src/server/intelligence/composition.ts, for exactly one registration. The Phase 19 report named the workflow_effect job handler a Phase 20 input, and the coordinator confirmed the defect: experience/workflows.ts already exports effectHandler() with the id workflow-effect, it is used only in a test, and it is NEVER registered with the worker. A deferred workflow therefore enqueues a workflow_effect wake-up job that the worker claims, cannot resolve a handler for, and fails TERMINALLY as unhandled_job, so the deferred workflow never resumes and every deferred workflow leaves a dead-lettered job behind. That would also make Phase 20 own operations runbook, which must document dead-letter retry, misleading. The coordinator granted three further paths after the candidate was reviewed: apps/web/src/server/intelligence/infrastructure/worker.ts, because the worker resolves a handler for seed_account, evaluate_trade and schedule_trigger only, so the retention job the phase delivered could never run; apps/web/src/server/intelligence/composition.ts, where the handlers are registered; and apps/web/src/app/api/intelligence/ as a directory, so the operator can reach the reset, the rebuild request and the retention run. The coordinator grants these because the phase acceptance cannot be demonstrated in production without them: a retention that never runs and an operator with no way to run it would leave the operations runbook describing something the operator cannot do.
